$description: Semantic tokens for the Lira for Professionals clinical app (lira-clinical-protocol). This records what that product actually is, rather than what we might one day want it to be. Distinct from pro-web.json, which is the /lira-for-professionals marketing page on the website.
$note: Values here are literal rather than references to tokens/primitives. The clinical app is built on Tailwind's own scales (slate, violet, emerald, amber, red, sky) and adopting them into the brand primitives would put a framework default next to the brand colours and blur both. Two colours are genuinely shared and are marked as such. The app does not import this file; it is the written record of its palette, and the CLAUDE.md in that repo carries the same table. If one changes, change the other.

strong.$description: slate-300. Panels asking for a decision

focus.$description: #ACDBC5, the brand mint, the mark in the v3 logo. Focus rings and form accents. The one brand colour this surface keeps

selected.$description: slate-700, --color-primary in globals.css. The chosen card in the wizard

focusOuter.$description: slate-900. O traço exterior do anel de foco. A menta sozinha dá 1,53:1 sobre branco e chumba o critério 1.4.11 da WCAG 2.1, que pede 3:1 para indicadores de foco. Com este traço por fora o anel passa a 17,85:1 e a menta continua a ser a cor da marca por dentro. O anel desenha-se com dois traços: menta a tocar o campo, este por fora

primary.$description: violet-600. The product accent: primary buttons, links, emphasis

state.$description: Each of these already means something. Check the meaning is free before using a colour for something new: a colour that says two things says neither.

inProgress.$description: amber. In progress, invite pending. Also the clinician's own amber on the ICSA crib sheet, so it is not free for anything else

risk.$description: red. Errors, destructive actions, and alerts the clinician flagged

shared.$description: sky. Shared with you by someone else

emphasis.$description: Two habits that keep the surface from drifting into the look of generated UI.

rule.$description: Do not use. A box with a tinted background, a coloured left bar and italic or bold text is the house style of generated UI; it reads as a warning or a decorative quote, and Lira never uses it, in any colour. The clinical app removed its last left rules on 2026-10-01; the entry stays as a record of what was there. Emphasis is plain text in the flow of the page

label.value: text label beside the note's author: {action.primaryHover} for pinned, {state.risk.fg} for alert
label.$description: How a pinned note or an alert the clinician raised is told apart from the others. The colour sits in the text of the label, never in a bar or a fill on the note

decision.$description: A panel asking the professional to decide something (is this the same person?) stays neutral. The violet button carries the action. It is a question, not an error. The background is slate-50, as in the app's two decision panels; it said slate-100 here until 2026-10-15, which the app never used. Spelt out under notice.decision

notice.$description: The four levels of every notice in the clinical app: warnings, strips, notes, status lines and form errors. Pick the level by what the professional has to do, not by how important the text feels. None of them uses a tinted box with a left bar, and none uses amber: amber is state.inProgress. A confirmation (Saved, Invite sent, All saved) is a note beside the button that did it, never green. Business rules (a limit, an account being verified, a link sent less than 30 days ago) are attention, never error. The state chips keep their own colours (state.*); blue is not a state and is not used.

note.$description: Information, nothing to do. Plain text next to the element it is about. No box, no background, no icon

attention.$description: Something to do, nothing is wrong. One line: a short label, the text, and a secondary button if there is an action. No background, no bar, no amber

letterSpacing.$description: tracking-wide, as every uppercase label in the app

padding.$description: py-1.5 px-3, as the app's other secondary buttons

decision.$description: The platform asks a question (is this the same person? export anyway?). The neutral panel of emphasis.decision, with the action in violet. It is never an error

error.$description: A failure, or a risk. Label and text in red. The box only when the error blocks the main action of the screen (the page did not load, the assessment could not be created); otherwise one line next to what failed

fontSize.$description: text-sm; the label as notice.attention.label, in red

border.$description: red-200. Not state.risk.border, which is the red-600 of a destructive button
